page.title: Hybrid Event Platforms Buyer Guide
page.description: Compare hybrid event platforms, decide format first, avoid late assets, and assign run‑of‑show ownership before you buy.
page.h1: What should you decide first about hybrid event platforms?
page.definition: Hybrid event platforms are software suites that let organisers run simultaneous in‑person and online experiences from a single dashboard. They combine streaming, registration, audience interaction, and analytics so producers can manage speakers, sponsors, and attendees without stitching together separate tools.
page.quick_answer: Pick the audience outcome and format before evaluating any platform, then assign a single owner for the run‑of‑show and lock the venue AV and streaming tool at least six weeks out.

sections.h2: Which audience outcome and format should drive the platform choice?

blocks.p: Start by defining the primary audience outcome and the event format because every platform excels at a different mix of live streaming, networking, and on‑demand delivery. If the goal is lead generation for a sales funnel, a webinar‑style platform with strong registration and CRM integration works best; if the goal is community building across time zones, a platform with persistent virtual rooms and chat threads is preferable.

ul: Identify whether the event is primarily broadcast, interactive, or hybrid networking
Match the format to platform strengths such as breakout rooms, exhibit halls, or live polling
Confirm the platform supports the required attendee capacity without extra fees
Verify integration points with marketing automation and CRM
Document the decision in a brief that the production team can reference

sections.h2: How early must you lock venue AV and the streaming platform?

blocks.p: Lock the venue AV contract and the streaming platform at least six weeks before the event date to give production time for rehearsals and contingency planning. Venue AV teams need lead time for rigging, signal routing, and on‑site testing, while the platform team must configure branding, registration pages, and backup streams.

ol: Confirm venue AV specifications and sign the contract
Select the streaming platform and provision the event instance
Create a shared run‑of‑show document with cue points
Schedule a full technical rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live
Run a final sixty‑minute technical check on event morning

sections.h2: What cost models exist for hybrid event platforms?

blocks.p: Hybrid platforms typically fall into three cost models that align with different budget cycles and scale requirements. Understanding the model helps you forecast total spend and avoid surprise overages.

sections.h2: Who owns the run‑of‑show and what does that include?

blocks.p: Assign a single run‑of‑show owner who is responsible for the cue sheet, speaker timing, backup stream, and live‑day communication. Without a named owner, cues slip, speakers run long, and the backup stream never gets tested.

ul: Maintain the master cue sheet with time codes
Coordinate speaker rehearsals and approve slide decks
Activate and monitor the backup stream throughout the event
Manage live Q&A moderation and audience chat
Deliver the edited recording and highlight clips within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours

sections.h2: What timeline and rehearsal cadence prevents last‑minute risk?

blocks.p: Follow a six‑to‑eight‑week timeline for conferences and a three‑to‑four‑week timeline for webinars, with a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live. Compressing the schedule forces shortcuts that surface as audio glitches, missed cues, or missing recordings.

ol: Kick‑off and scope definition week one
Platform configuration and branding week two
Speaker briefs and slide collection week three
Full technical rehearsal week four or five
Live event execution and post‑event delivery week six to eight

faq.q: Can I use a single platform for both virtual and in‑person components?
faq.a: Yes, most enterprise suites let you manage a physical venue feed and a virtual audience from one dashboard, but you still need separate AV crews and a backup stream for each feed. Plan for distinct encoding paths and test both paths during the full rehearsal.

faq.q: What is the typical production cost range for a moderated webinar?
faq.a: West Peek Productions publishes a directional range of $2,500 to $7,500 per moderated webinar production, covering producer, backup stream, and edited recording; actual cost depends on speaker count and branding complexity. The fee also includes a live Q&A moderator and a post‑event clip package.

faq.q: How many weeks should I plan for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: A hybrid conference typically needs six to eight weeks of preparation, including venue AV contracts, platform setup, speaker rehearsals, and a full technical run‑through before the live day. Build in buffer days for unexpected venue changes and for the post‑event recording delivery window.

faq.q: What should I include in a run‑of‑show document?
faq.a: A run‑of‑show lists every cue with time codes, speaker names, slide transitions, video rolls, poll launches, and backup‑stream triggers, plus contact numbers for the producer, AV lead, and platform operator. Attach the final approved script and a contingency plan for connectivity loss.
